title: Values that leave the process: translating one corrupts data, and no gate would catch it

census.why: The AST tier has to be the one reading this, or container semantics — enum member, switch case, comparison operand — are unavailable and every string below becomes a guess.
Same, and the tagged templates need the tag name to be readable.
Present so the case carries one thing that genuinely must be translated; a corpus of pure refusals proves only that the tool says no.

expectations.why: A persisted status union. Translate one member and every row already in the database stops parsing — silently, at read time, long after the commit.
An enum's VALUE is the wire format; only its name is for people. The two sit one token apart and look alike.
A localStorage key that happens to contain a French word. Translating it orphans every existing user's saved draft — the data is still there and the application can no longer find it.
A discriminant compared against a value the sender chose. The string beside it in the same function IS copy, which is what makes position, not appearance, the only reliable signal.
Compared, never rendered. An extractor reading values without their containers cannot tell this from a label.
A media type. It is negotiated with a server that has never heard of French.
Every identifier inside a GraphQL document belongs to the schema. `title` here is a field name, and the same word three lines away in a component would be a label.
Same argument, different embedded language. Translating a column name turns a query into a runtime error nobody sees until production.
A validator's literal is the accepted input, not a message. Translating it rejects every request that was previously valid.

The whole point of the case. This one string is both the persisted value and the rendered label, and the two want opposite treatment. Refusing — loudly, so somebody decides — is the only correct answer; guessing either way corrupts something.
Real copy, returned from the same switch whose cases must not move. A tool that refuses this file wholesale is as wrong as one that translates all of it.
Copy sitting in the same module as two embedded query languages.

expectations.find: Un atelier de publication pour petites équipes
expectations.why: Rendered on npmjs.com. Cited to a rule, so the verdict is traceable to documented evidence rather than to the string looking like a sentence.
A dependency range, one line from a field that must be translated. The companion matchers in the same rule are what keep them apart.

knownGaps: `'Synchronisation en cours'` comes back needs-judgment/no-rule while `'Réinitialisation demandée'`, its sibling in the same switch, comes back translate. Same position, same shape, two answers. Not asserted either way here: pinning the inconsistent pair would make it look decided.

`'email'` and `'push'` — the Channel enum VALUES — land on needs-judgment/short-string rather than enum-member, so they are refused for the right outcome by the wrong reason. Only their brevity saves them; a longer enum value in the same position reads as copy.
